name: Ingogo
body:
INGOGO
CR 2

This squat humanoid is covered with shaggy gray fur all over its body and a narrow tail, but its face is nearly human aside form its simian jaws and long fangs.

XP 600
NE Medium humanoid
Init +1; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +2

DEFENSE

AC 13, touch 11, flat-footed 12 (+1 Dex, +2 natural)
hp 13 (2d8+4)
Fort +5, Ref +1, Will +0

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., climb 15 ft.
Melee bite +3 (1d4+2 plus poison) or slam +3 (1d4+2 plus grab)
Ranged thrown objects +2 (1d4+2 plus fling filth)
Special Attacks dirty fighting

STATISTICS

Str 14, Dex 12, Con 14, Int 7, Wis 11, Cha 11
Base Atk +1; CMB +3 (+7 grapple); CMD 14
Feats Throw Anything
Skills Climb +10, Perception +2
Languages Common

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Dirty Fighting (Ex)

An ingogo has +2 circumstance bonus on attack rolls against grappled creatures.

Fling Filth (Ex)

An ingogo can use almost anything as a ranged weapon, but as a swift action can smear any object it throws with its own filth. A creature struck by its thrown object is sickened by this filth for 1d3 rounds (DC 13 Fort negates). The save DC is Constitution-based.

Poison (Ex)

Bite—injury; save Fort DC 13; frequency 1/round for 4 rounds; effect 1d2 Dexterity damage; cure 1 save.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, gang (3-6), or mob (7-20 with 2-3 leaders with fighter, barbarian, or rogue levels)
Treasure standard

The ingogo, which resemble a cross between humans and baboons, able to speak but tend only to shout and scream in vulgar language. The ingogo are medium sized, walk on all fours and have tails, but their faces closely resemble human faces.

The ingogo are notorious for their vicious attacks, eschewing weapons and preferring to use their hands to grab their prey, then bite them viciously as their numbers overwhelm their victims. If their victim is too far to reach, they will gladly throw whatever is in reach to pelt their target until it either runs away or is Incapacitated. Known to smear waste on their weapons, even light scratches from ingogo attacks can become a liability.

The ingogo is said to be second in obnoxiousness to only the getiet. Ingogo are constant pests, driving off wildlife, causing cattle stampedes, stealing valuables, waylaying travelers, screaming at night, and they know more curse words than most humans will ever hear in a lifetime.

Cowardly when alone, they will quickly run away to return with a larger group to bully other creatures.
